units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 99">Gen. R. s. 99</cite>, end (ref. to <he>כאחד</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 49:16">Gen. XLIX, 16</cite>) <he>כִּיחִידוֹ של וכ׳</he> (not <he>כיחודו</he>) like the Only One of the world, as He needs no help &c.; <cite ref="Genesis 49:16">ib.</cite> s. 21 (ref. to <he>כאחד</he>, ib. III, 22). Ib. s. 55 <he>זה י׳ לאמו וכ׳</he> this one (Ishmael) is the only son of his mother, and the other (Isaac) is &c.—
<cite ref="Taanit 9a:8">Taan. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>בשביל י׳</he> for an individual’s sake, opp. <he>רבים</he>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 9a">Ber. 9ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>י׳ ורבים הלכה וכ׳</he> where a single opinion is opposed to the opinion of more than one, the law follows the latter.
<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 5:5">Bets. V, 5</cite> <he>בור של י׳</he> a well belonging to an individual.
<cite ref="Eruvin 46a:20">Erub. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>י׳ במקום י׳</he> an individual opinion opposed to an individual opinion; a. v. fr.—
Y. Keth. VII, 31ᵇ bot. בְּיָ׳ (= בְּיִחוּד) privately.—Pl. יְחִידִים, יְחִידִין.
R. Hash. 17ᵇ כי׳ דמי are to be considered as individuals (in prayer); a. fr.—Fem. יְחִידָה.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> <he>בת י׳</he> an only daughter; a. fr.—

Deut. R. s. 2, end מה הקב״ה … כך הנפש י׳ בגוף as the Lord is matchless in his world, so is the soul in the body; Midr. Till. to Ps. CIII; Gen. R. s. 14, end שכל האברים … והיא י׳ בגוף all limbs are paired, but she (the soul) is unmatched in the body.—As a noun (b. h.) יְחִידָה soul.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 14">Ib.</cite> Deut. R. l. c.; a. e.

senses.gloss: select, esp. one devoted to a particularly scrupulous life.
units: Taan. 10ᵇ איזהו י׳ who is called a yaḥid? Ans. י׳ כל שראוי וכ׳ whoever is worthy to be appointed manager of a community.

Ib. אל יאמר אדם … להיות י׳ one must not say, I am only a student, I am not fit to lead the life of a yaḥid (it would be an assumption, v. יוֹהֲרָא); Tosef. ib. I, 7 (v. Var. in ed. Zuck. a. Rabb. D. S. to Taan. l. c.); Y. Ber. II, end, 5ᵈ כל דבר של צער … י׳ עושה in all matters of self-abnegation, whoever desires to make himself a yaḥid, may do so.—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 1:4">Taan. I, 4</cite>; a. fr. V. <cite ref="J00287"><he>יְחִידִי</he></cite>
